description: Somos un equipo en busca de conocer y desarrollar herramientas que permitan la implementación de datos para la creación de un ecosistema educativo y dinámico... ¿estás listo?
summary:
A video game whose main goal is to provide an immersive experience so that young players can learn more about missions that, although they have reached the end of their operational life, have not been forgotten. The data collected continues to help scientists better understand the Moon, Mars, and deep space.
Through this game, we achieve the challenge’s goal by bringing those missions back to life. In this way, future generations will learn just how much these man-made objects have contributed to our view and understanding of the universe, and they will continue to serve as a valuable source of information—not only through the data they’ve collected but also by demonstrating how to maintain probes and rovers beyond their standard operational lifespans.
details:
What does it do or how does it work? The game allows the player to take on the role of three avatars (probes or robots). Each avatar is equipped with measurement tools that provide the player with relevant data for each of the missions.

What benefits does it have? Thanks to this game, our players have a great time while learning. Nowadays, we should take advantage of new technologies to provide people with information that would have been more difficult to explain in the past.

What is the intended impact of the project? To bring young people a bit of the human history related to our expansion into the cosmos and don´t let this past missions and their discoveries been forgotten.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project? We used Google’s Gemini tool to draft the code in JSON format, and the Claude program to execute it. Our work focused on gathering information from the various tools provided as part of the challenge. Afterward, we organized a database that could enhance our avatars. From the vast amount of available information, we determined which data to use.

How is your project creative? Because the game allows the player command the probes or robot. It´s a game open to the general public and a spectacular way to talk about these missions.

What factors did your team consider? We had to consider which missions we would talk about, how we would go about it and what we would say.
